newsitem.title: ABU DHABI: Abu Dhabi to step up oil drilling activity.
newsitem.headline: Abu Dhabi to step up oil drilling activity.

text.p: Oil drilling in the Gulf Arab emirate of Abu Dhabi will be stepped up over the next four years to ensure the long-term productivity of its reservoirs, managers at operating firms in Abu Dhabi said on Tuesday.

Abu Dhabi Company for Onshore Oil Operations (ADCO), the country's largest operator with an output of one million barrels per day (bpd), will increase the number of wells drilled from 99 this year to 103 in 1997 and to 131 by the year 2000, ADCO drilling manager Richard Reiley told an industry conference.
ADCO's activities centre on the producing Bab, Bu Hasa, Asab, Sahil and Shah fields. The last three are being developed further to offset declines at other wells.
The major component of ADCO's programme will be workover wells but it also plans to use extensive horizontal development drilling over the next two years to exploit onshore reserves.
"Though they (horizontal wells) cost more, the price per barrel is less," Reiley said.
Horizontal wells will rise from 16 this year to 33 next year, 44 in 1998 before falling back to 41 in 1999.
Workovers will range between 33 and 25 a year between 1997 and the year 2000.
No exploration wells are planned to be drilled by ADCO in 1997 and only two will be sunk in 1998.

ADCO, 60 percent state owned and 40 percent by foreign firms, is doing specification planning work on increasing the number of its rigs it operates from the National Drilling Company from 11 to 12 in 1998, Reiley said.
Drilling at offshore depoists is also set to rise.

Offshore oil operator Abu Dhabi Marine Operating Company (ADMA-OPCO) will utilise its 10 rigs to drill 64 wells in 1997 and 51 wells in 1998, Ahmed Al Muhairy, in charge of ADMA-OPCO drilling operations said.

Abu Dhabi accounts for more than 90 percent of the 2.16 million barrels per day (bpd) produced by OPEC member United Arab Emirates (UAE) and is one of only a few OPEC states currently with spare production capacity.
Abu Dhabi has proven recoverable oil reserves of around 98 billion barrels, the world's fourth largest after Saudi Arabia, Iraq and Iran, official UAE estimates show.
